claims.text: Beside the prompt and the vendor's system prompt, an agent should take an Agent Behaviour Policy written to a published standard, which the vendor accepts, enforces as far as it can, and eventually answers for.
claims.quote: It should also get an Agent Behaviour Policy, written to a published standard, which the vendor accepts, enforces as far as it can, and eventually answers for.

claims.text: Language models do not separate code from data: every instruction and every piece of content arrives in the same channel.
claims.quote: They do not separate code from data.

claims.text: The NCSC said in December 2025 that current models simply do not enforce a security boundary between instructions and data, and Simon Willison's phrase is that LLMs follow instructions in content.
claims.quote: simply do not enforce a security boundary between instructions and data inside a prompt

claims.text: A behaviour policy does not fix that; it takes the most important instructions out of the channel anybody can write into, loaded by the platform, versioned, signed and checked outside the model where it can be.
claims.quote: What it does is take the most important instructions out of the channel that anybody can write into.

claims.text: Claude Code's own documentation says its permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model.
claims.quote: are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model

claims.text: Agent behaviour is becoming an existential threat to the model companies, through liability and above all through trust: a decent number of people badly hurt is enough for many more to stop giving agents instructions.
claims.quote: I think agent behaviour is becoming an existential threat to the companies that make the models

claims.text: From 9 December 2026 software, AI systems included, is a product under the EU's new product liability rules.
claims.quote: from 9 December 2026 software, AI systems included, is a product under the EU's new product liability rules

claims.text: At 1995's rate of 2.72 fatal airliner accidents per million flights, 2025's 38.7 million flights would have produced about 105 fatal accidents; the Aviation Safety Network counted 12.
claims.quote: At the 1995 rate, that is about 105 fatal accidents in a year, two a week.

value.unit: fatal airliner accidents 2025 would have had at the 1995 rate, against 12 counted

claims.text: Aviation did not get safe out of altruism; it got safe because everybody knew every crash anywhere would be news, and an industry with two fatal crashes a week would not have its passengers.
claims.quote: It got there because everybody knew that every crash, anywhere in the world, would be news

claims.text: Card payments have had some of the best security teams and fraud detection anywhere because the liability was moved onto the companies.
claims.quote: Very simple: the liability was moved onto the companies.

claims.text: Consumers stopped carrying the loss: in the United States since 1970 a cardholder is liable for unauthorised use only up to $50, and in the UK up to £35 for a lost or stolen card.
claims.quote: only if... the liability is not in excess of $50

value.unit: USD cap on a cardholder's liability

claims.text: In October 2015 US counterfeit fraud liability shifted to whoever had not adopted chip cards, and the PCI Security Standards Council, founded in 2006 by the card brands, wrote the industry's own standard.
claims.quote: The industry wrote its own standard.

claims.text: Since October 2024 UK payment providers must reimburse authorised push payment scam victims up to £85,000; 88% of money lost was reimbursed in the first 18 months and losses over Faster Payments fell around 21%.
claims.quote: losses sent over Faster Payments fell by around 21%

value.unit: percent fall in APP scam losses over Faster Payments

claims.text: The parties carrying the loss built the detection: Target learned of its 2013 breach from the Department of Justice, and Verizon found almost all point-of-sale breaches were reported to the victim by third parties.
claims.quote: The parties carrying the loss had built the detection.

claims.text: Regulation alone does not do it: Meta's €1.2 billion GDPR fine in 2023 was the largest at the time, and in 2025 the European Commission fined it €200 million over its consent-or-pay model.
claims.quote: in 2023 was the largest at the time, and in 2025 the European Commission

claims.text: Real improvement came where three things lined up: a rule, a liability that landed on the company, and a systemic risk to the business model the company could see.
claims.quote: a rule, a liability that landed on the company, and a systemic risk to the business model that the company could see

claims.text: The split: the rows the vendor accepted, the vendor keeps and answers for if they break; everything the policy does not cover stays with the user, and the vendors that keep more rows as boundaries can sell that as the product.
claims.quote: The rows the vendor accepted, the vendor keeps, and answers for if they break.

claims.text: As Hope or enforcement measured, the share of a policy that rests on hope can fall from 97% to 23% with the right design, and the vendors can make the next part of that fall.
claims.quote: can fall from 97% to 23% with the right design

value.unit: percent of a policy resting on hope, after against before

claims.text: The standard needs five things: a versioned signed policy file, the vendor's acknowledgement per row, the vendor's own policy in the same format, a same-day breach report, and liability per row starting with the boundaries.
claims.quote: A versioned policy file, with the reach, the mandate, the gap and the barriers, row by row, signed by the deployer

claims.text: Today the policy travels inside what we already provide: over the API in our system prompt, since Anthropic's app system prompts do not apply to the API; in the Claude apps and Claude Code after the vendor's own.
claims.quote: The behaviour policy goes there, after the vendor's.

claims.text: In both modes today the system prompt and the behaviour policy are almost pure hope; Anthropic says CLAUDE.md files are context, not enforced configuration, and a PreToolUse hook is what blocks an action.
claims.quote: In both modes, today, the system prompt and our behaviour policy are almost pure hope.

claims.text: Vendors already run checks outside the model where they care, such as Claude in Chrome's safety classifier; the behaviour policy deserves the same machinery, with its rows controlled by the deployer.
claims.quote: The behaviour policy deserves the same machinery, with one difference: the policy's rows should be controlled by us.

claims.text: A system prompt is a light behaviour policy already and should be written as one, layered: the vendor's published policy, then the deployer's with the business rules only the deployer can write.
claims.quote: a system prompt is a light version of one already: it tells the agent how to behave

claims.text: Most agents already run a policy we cannot see: Claude in Chrome will not type a password, is prohibited from stock trading and bypassing captchas, and asks before financial sites.
claims.quote: That is a policy, and a good one

claims.text: Reverse-engineer the policies agents already run, as the Gmail connector's thirty tools were measured, and publish them in the ABP format; the gap between measured and published is a finding.
claims.quote: If the vendors will not publish their policies yet, the measured ones are the next best thing, and the gap between the two is a finding.

claims.text: The confidence question is open: no published figures for how often a model keeps a system prompt or policy under pressure, and no model reports its confidence rule by rule.
claims.quote: The confidence question is open.

claims.text: It is a proposal: no vendor accepts a behaviour policy as an input today in this sense; Claude Code's permission rules and managed settings are the nearest thing and cover settings, not business rules.
claims.quote: No vendor accepts a behaviour policy as an input today in the sense described

claims.text: A policy does not separate code from data; it moves the most important instructions into a channel the content cannot reach, and prompt injection remains.
claims.quote: A policy does not separate code from data.

claims.text: The aviation numbers mix sources: the 1995 rate is the Aviation Safety Network's over ICAO departures via Our World in Data, the 2025 count is ASN's and the flights are IATA's.
claims.quote: The aviation numbers mix sources.

claims.text: The payments history is short and partial: fraud did not disappear, it moved, and the 21% fall is one evaluation's estimate.
claims.quote: The payments history is short and partial.

claims.text: That it does not take many users being hurt to lose public trust is the owner's judgement, with no number for how many incidents it takes.
claims.quote: I have no number for how many incidents it takes to lose public trust in agents.

claims.text: Liability per row is the end state, not the start; acknowledgement and breach reporting can come first.
claims.quote: Liability per row is the end state, not the start.

claims.text: The idea came up while the owner was answering Ralf Thomas on where the liability line should fall, and deserves to stand as its own proposal.
claims.quote: I think it deserves to be its own proposal, put out there on its own

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 13 October 2026 and a second memo the same evening, written by the site's agent in the voice of the site; the argument and editorial responsibility are the owner's.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 13 October 2026
